key_idea: Three-in-a-row on a large board is won on move 3: make an open pair in a direction whose two extension cells and far cell are untouched by the opponent's single stone, then take whichever end is not blocked.
sketch: Play the centre (30,21). After the opponent's reply pick one of the 8 directions d such that centre-d, centre+d and centre+2d are all free of the opponent's stone, and play centre+d. This creates two winning cells (centre-d and centre+2d); the opponent has only one stone so cannot threaten anything and can block only one end, and we win with the other. Constant time. Pitfalls: flush after each line, handle '0 0', and choose the direction after seeing the reply (a direction always exists since one stone blocks at most a few of 8). Interactive, so the sample checker cannot judge it; samples_passed is true because my own local interactor (win/illegal/loss detection, all opponent first replies within 3 cells of the centre times blocking strategies, plus random ones) always reported a win on move 3.
